title: False Positive
novel: Marshall and Lily received [[shocking|shock]] news that Lily might be pregnant. They were [[overjoyed|overjoyed]] and started planning for the baby immediately. Marshall bought a crib, painted the nursery, and even started reading baby name books. Lily called her mother and shared the [[exciting|excite]] news. However, a follow-up test revealed that it was a false [[positive|positive]]. The pregnancy test had been wrong. Marshall and Lily were [[devastated|devastate]]. They had already let themselves dream about their future child, and now that dream was [[shattered|shatter]]. They held each other and cried in the empty nursery. Meanwhile, Robin got a new job as a morning show host. She was [[thrilled|thrill]] at first, but she quickly realized that the job required her to do [[humiliating|humiliate]] stunts and wear silly costumes. She felt like she was going [[backward|backward]] in her career. Barney, on the other hand, discovered the joy of giving on Christmas. He [[donated|donate]] a large sum of money to a charity and felt a warmth he had never [[experienced|experience]] before. He was so moved that he tried to [[replicate|replicate]] the feeling by giving even more. However, his [[generosity|generosity]] quickly got out of hand, and he ended up [[bankrupting|bankrupt]] himself. Ted tried to help his friends through their [[respective|respective]] crises. He told Marshall and Lily that they would have a baby when the time was right. He encouraged Robin to keep [[pushing|push]] forward in her career. And he helped Barney understand that giving did not mean giving everything away. By the end of the episode, everyone found a small piece of [[hope|hope]] in their difficult situations. The gang gathered at MacLaren's and toasted to the future, agreeing that even false positives could lead to [[genuine|genuine]] growth.

shock.en: to cause someone to feel very surprised

excite.en: to make someone feel eager and happy

positive.en: a result that shows something is present

devastate.en: to cause someone great sadness or shock

shatter.en: to break suddenly into small pieces

thrill.en: to make someone feel very excited

humiliate.en: to make someone feel deeply ashamed

donate.en: to give money or goods to help others

experience.en: to live through an event or feeling

replicate.en: to do or make something again in the same way

generosity.en: the quality of giving freely to others

bankrupt.en: to make someone unable to pay debts

push.en: to force or encourage something forward

hope.en: a feeling that good things will happen
